issue.title: bob periods brief Bryan's words duplicates Work Log lines, truncates later days, sorts by link text, and mangles link-only notes

task_type_fields.impact: Drafters lose the second half of the week's verbatim quotes and must work around corrupted link text. The Review rule 'quote Bryan only verbatim, with a link' becomes unsafe.
task_type_fields.repro:
`bob periods brief 2026-W37 -f md` shows exactly 40 `## Bryan's words` entries (Sep 7: 11, Sep 8: 7, Sep 9: 22) and none for Thu Sep 10 – Sun Sep 13. W36 and W35 also stop at exactly 40, losing the last days. Four defects in `bryans_words_section` / `pomodoro_notes`:
1. **Duplicates + truncation** (bob-cli-gr.7 note #1): `work_log_entries` (a task's mirrored WORK LOG, linked as `done/bob_done` with no block anchor) and `pomodoro_notes` (the daily-note Pomodoro child) both emit the same line. Nothing dedups them before `truncate(40)`.
2. **Order** (bob-cli-gr.12 note #1): the sort key is `(date, link)`, so same-day entries come out alphabetical by link text. W32 Aug 9 shows 0920, then 1605, then 0725. Sort by date only, with a stable sort.
3. **Mangled bare links** (bob-cli-gr.10 note #1): `trim_start_matches(['[', ']', 'x', ' '])` strips the `[[` from a link-only child such as `- [[sase_better_tasks]]` (2026/20260817), which yields `[[2026/20260817|sase_better_tasks]]]]`. The same trim eats a leading `x` from real notes ("xprompt …"). Trim only a checkbox prefix, and skip children that are only a wiki-link.
4. **Nested links** (bob-cli-gr.17 note #2): a W27 line containing `[[sase]]` renders as the stray fragment `[[2026/20260629|sase]]]] · sase]]` because `note_link` nests the raw text inside an alias. Strip or escape wiki-links in alias text.
Fix: dedup by (date, text) and prefer the block-anchored daily-note link. Cap per day, or report what was cut.

issue.creation_reason: Four bob-cli-gr phase agents (gr.7 #1, gr.10 #1, gr.12 #1, gr.17 #2) each hit a different defect in the brief's Bryan's words section while drafting W37, W34, W32, and W27. All four sit in the same two functions.
